title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 2
paragraphs: This, the Persians say, is how Io came to Egypt — though the Hellenes tell it differently — and this, according to them, was the first injury. Afterwards, they say, some Hellenes (whose nationality they cannot name) put in at the Phoenician city of Tyre and carried off the king's daughter Europa. These must have been Cretans, and so the two sides were even. But after this, they say, the Hellenes committed the second wrong. They sailed in a warship to Aia in Colchis and up the river Phasis, and after completing the other business that had brought them there, they carried off the king's daughter Medea. The king of Colchis sent a herald to Hellas demanding satisfaction for the abduction and the return of his daughter. The Hellenes replied that since the barbarians had given no satisfaction for the abduction of Io the Argive, they would give none for Medea either.
